headline: TCU LEADS A RESHAPED BCS PLAYOFF RACE
body_markdown:
Season 2 has reached Week 12 with a new team atop the CFP rankings, Oklahoma finally beaten and several contenders carrying their best football into the stretch run.

TCU leads the published Week 12 CFP order at 9–1. California is second, Notre Dame third, Texas A&M fourth, LSU fifth and Florida sixth. Oklahoma and Texas round out the top eight.

**TCU AND CALIFORNIA SET THE PACE**

The Horned Frogs have won seven straight since their 35–7 loss to LSU. Their résumé includes a 38–31 victory over California, the only defeat on the Golden Bears’ 10–1 schedule.

TCU’s recent run has required precision in close games: 27–21 over Michigan, 29–24 over Miami and 34–31 over Baylor. California has taken a different route, winning nine consecutive games and closing its latest outing with a 52–17 victory over Missouri. J. Sagapolutele threw for 453 yards and six touchdowns in that win.

**ARKANSAS CHANGES OKLAHOMA’S SEASON**

Oklahoma won its first nine games, including five opening victories by at least 49 points each. The Sooners beat Texas A&M 35–14, Florida 65–38 and LSU 43–42 before Arkansas ended the unbeaten run with a 57–55 Week 11 upset.

The Razorbacks are 6–4 and have scored 106 points across consecutive wins over Kansas State and Oklahoma. The Sooners remain 9–1, but enter Week 12 seventh in the CFP rankings.

**NOTRE DAME’S EIGHT-WIN RESPONSE**

The Irish lost their first two games to Florida and Texas A&M. They have won every completed game since.

Notre Dame is now 8–2 after beating Washington 63–31. Its surge has included one-score victories over Houston, Alabama and USC, followed by a 59–18 win over Ohio State.

Jonaz Walton supplied one of the season’s standout performances against Virginia Tech: 311 rushing yards and seven touchdowns in a 66–28 victory.

**THE SEC CONTENDERS KEEP ANSWERING**

Texas A&M, LSU and Florida each stand at 8–2.

The Aggies have won three straight, most recently beating Georgia 31–27. Earlier, Marcel Reed threw six touchdown passes and added three rushing scores in a 66–24 win over Arkansas.

LSU answered its one-point Oklahoma loss by beating Miami 71–55. Harlem Berry produced 329 combined rushing and receiving yards and four touchdowns. Miami’s Girard Pringle Jr. countered with 417 combined yards and five scores, earning National and ACC offensive honors despite the defeat.

Florida has responded to its Oklahoma loss with wins over Kansas State and Georgia by a combined 97–44.

**TEXAS AND OHIO STATE BUILD LATE MOMENTUM**

Texas has won four straight to reach 8–2, including a 17–13 win over Pittsburgh. Ohio State has won three consecutive games and stands at 6–4 after beating Louisville 49–25.

Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 201 yards and four touchdowns against Louisville. He heads the Week 12 Heisman watch, followed by Malachi Coleman, Walton and Micah Hudson.

Elsewhere, Virginia Tech’s five interceptions helped end a four-game skid against Alabama, while Houston snapped an eight-game losing streak with a 20–14 win over Oregon.

Week 12 brings LSU–Florida, Texas–Miami, Oklahoma–Georgia and TCU–Pittsburgh. The next results will test a playoff picture that has already changed substantially.

*Season 2 / 2027, entering Week 12. As of November 1, 2026. Records reflect completed schedules; rankings are the published Week 12 CFP rankings.*

headline: LSU BEATS FLORIDA, SETS UP NINE-WIN SHOWDOWN WITH TEXAS A&M
body_markdown:
LSU has answered its narrowest defeat with two victories—and now has another nine-win opponent waiting.

The Tigers beat Florida 45–35 in Week 12, improving to 9–2 through their completed schedule and setting up a Week 13 meeting with Texas A&M. The Aggies also reached 9–2 by beating Kansas State 35–13, extending their winning streak to four games.

LSU and Florida entered their matchup fifth and sixth, respectively, in the published Week 12 CFP rankings. Those positions preceded the result. The Tigers now have a win over the Gators to add to their résumé, while Florida stands at 8–3.

The victory continues LSU’s response to its 43–42 loss to Oklahoma in Week 9. After beating Miami 71–55, the Tigers followed with another 45 points against Florida. Across those two wins, LSU has scored 116 points.

That response matters in a season with little room between the leading contenders. LSU has won five of its last six completed games, with the one-point Oklahoma defeat its only loss in that stretch. Its next opponent brings a sustained run of its own.

Texas A&M’s four consecutive victories have come against Arkansas, South Carolina, Georgia and Kansas State. The Aggies have outscored those opponents 180–76, moving beyond their Week 7 loss to Oklahoma and into a consequential meeting with LSU.

The published Week 12 CFP order lists Texas A&M fourth and LSU fifth. Their upcoming game gives both teams a direct opportunity to strengthen their position against another contender.

Oklahoma, meanwhile, supplied its own emphatic response in Week 12. The Sooners beat Georgia 63–9 after their first defeat of the season against Arkansas. Oklahoma is now 10–1; Georgia fell to 6–5.

Florida’s next scheduled opponent is Florida State. The Gators had beaten Kansas State and Georgia in consecutive games before LSU ended that run.

For the Tigers, the Florida result turns an anticipated matchup into a completed statement. Texas A&M is next, with both teams carrying nine victories into the meeting.

headline: CALIFORNIA REACHES 11 WINS, SAGAPOLUTELE THROWS SIX MORE TOUCHDOWNS
body_markdown:
California extended its winning streak to 10 games with a 56–40 Week 12 victory over Stanford, improving to 11–1 through its completed schedule.

J. Sagapolutele completed 22 of 30 passes for 484 yards and six touchdowns with one interception. He has thrown six touchdown passes in each of California’s last two games, following the 52–17 win over Missouri.

The scoring throws were divided evenly among three receivers. V. Spafford caught six passes for 144 yards and two touchdowns, M. Danzy added six catches for 103 yards and two scores, and D. Thomas finished with four catches for 82 yards and two touchdowns.

J. Napier led California with 146 receiving yards on five catches. J. Wagoner added an interception on defense.

The Golden Bears have won every game since their Week 2 loss to TCU. Their published Week 12 CFP listing placed them second before the Stanford result.

headline: JACKSON SCORES THREE AS OHIO STATE WINS FOURTH STRAIGHT
body_markdown:
Ohio State won its fourth consecutive game by beating Virginia Tech 49–35 in Week 12, improving to 7–4 through its completed schedule.

B. Jackson contributed three touchdowns and 148 combined rushing and receiving yards. He carried 16 times for 82 yards and two scores, then caught six passes for 66 yards and another touchdown.

Jeremiah Smith added six catches for 88 yards and a touchdown. The Buckeyes also received a touchdown catch from C. Henry Jr. and a rushing score from A. Rogers.

Ohio State’s defense intercepted three passes: two by K. Harris and one by D. Kelly. Z. Elee recorded two sacks as the Buckeyes finished with four.

Virginia Tech countered with eight catches for 273 yards and three touchdowns from Q. Brown, but fell to 3–8.

Ohio State’s winning streak now includes Washington, Oregon, Louisville and Virginia Tech.

headline: NO. 1 TCU, NO. 7 TEXAS CARRY WINNING STREAKS INTO ACC SHOWDOWN
body_markdown:
TCU has won eight straight. Texas has won five. Their next game puts those streaks—and two unbeaten conference records—against each other.

The Horned Frogs enter Week 13 at 10–1 and No. 1 in the published CFP rankings after beating Pittsburgh 38–17. Texas is 9–2 and seventh after a 38–24 victory over Miami. Both teams stand at 6–0 in completed ACC games, with TCU scheduled to visit the Longhorns next.

TCU’s latest win supplied a cleaner margin after several narrow finishes. C. Berger completed 17 of 19 passes for 265 yards and four touchdowns without an interception against Pittsburgh.

E. Small caught three passes for 99 yards and two scores. D. Jones added four catches for 79 yards and a touchdown, while K. Pimpton supplied the other touchdown reception. J. Denman contributed a rushing score and 108 combined rushing and receiving yards.

For a team that beat Miami by five points and Baylor by three, the 21-point victory gives TCU a more comfortable result before its next ranked opponent.

Texas brought an efficient passing performance of its own to the Miami game. A. Manning completed 20 of 29 throws for 296 yards and four touchdowns without an interception.

K. Lockett handled half of those completions, finishing with 10 catches for 134 yards and two touchdowns. C. Coleman added 93 receiving yards and a score, and N. Townsend caught the remaining touchdown pass.

The Longhorns’ defense intercepted two passes, one each by X. Filsaime and K. Black. Texas has now won every completed game since its Week 6 loss to Oklahoma, building a five-game run that includes consecutive victories over Pittsburgh and Miami.

TCU’s streak stretches back further. The Horned Frogs have won every game since their Week 3 loss to LSU, and their résumé includes California’s only defeat.

Now the two ACC contenders meet directly. TCU brings the top CFP position and a chance to reach 11 wins. Texas brings home field, its strongest sustained run of the season and an opportunity to beat the team atop the rankings.

headline: WALTON RUNS FOR 304 YARDS, FIVE TOUCHDOWNS IN NINTH STRAIGHT IRISH WIN
body_markdown:
Jonaz Walton ran for 304 yards and five touchdowns as Notre Dame beat Oregon 56–21 in Week 12, extending its winning streak to nine games.

Walton carried 28 times, averaging 10.9 yards per attempt, and added a 10-yard reception. The performance earned him Big Ten offensive player-of-the-week honors.

T. Mobley supplied another 104 rushing yards and two touchdowns on nine carries. Together, the two backs accounted for 408 rushing yards and seven scores.

Notre Dame’s defense recorded eight sacks, including three by F. Brewu and two by J. Ausberry. Ausberry also intercepted a pass.

The Irish are now 9–2 through their completed schedule after opening the season with losses to Florida and Texas A&M. Their published Week 13 CFP listing places them fourth, while Walton holds the second spot in the current Heisman watch. Stanford is next on Notre Dame’s schedule.

headline: COLEMAN DELIVERS CONSECUTIVE SEVEN-TOUCHDOWN RECEIVING GAMES
body_markdown:
Malachi Coleman has followed one seven-touchdown receiving performance with another.

The Oklahoma receiver caught 10 passes for 282 yards and seven touchdowns in a 93–28 Week 13 win over Kansas State. That came after 11 catches for 348 yards and seven scores against Georgia in Week 12.

Across those two games, Coleman produced 21 receptions, 630 yards and 14 receiving touchdowns. His Georgia performance earned National offensive player-of-the-week honors, and the published Week 13 Heisman watch lists him first.

Oklahoma improved to 11–1 through its completed schedule. The Sooners have answered their two-point loss to Arkansas with wins over Georgia and Kansas State by a combined 156–37.

T. Keys added six catches for 265 yards and two touchdowns against Kansas State, while K. Kasper caught five passes for 119 yards and two scores.

Coleman’s latest performance gives an already extraordinary two-game stretch another seven-touchdown entry.

headline: TCU PICKS OFF FIVE, BEATS TEXAS 38–14
body_markdown:
TCU’s meeting with Texas began as a matchup of long winning streaks and unbeaten ACC records. The Horned Frogs left with both of theirs intact.

TCU beat Texas 38–14 in Week 13, intercepting five passes and getting three rushing touchdowns from A. Henderson. The victory extended the Horned Frogs’ winning streak to nine games and improved their completed-schedule record to 11–1.

Texas fell to 9–3, with its five-game winning streak ending against the team listed first in the published Week 13 CFP rankings. The Longhorns entered the matchup seventh. Those rankings preceded the result.

The difference was substantial on both sides of the ball. Henderson carried 21 times for 103 yards and three scores, then added a 26-yard reception. His production gave TCU a dependable scoring source in a game that required only 14 passing attempts from C. Berger.

Berger completed 10 of those throws for 125 yards and a touchdown without an interception. T. Shelton caught the scoring pass and finished with three receptions for 43 yards. D. Jones added five catches for 54 yards.

TCU’s defense supplied the takeaways. M. Strickland intercepted two passes, while M. Teason, E. Hill IV and K. Jackson each added one. C. Buck recorded two sacks and J. Battle added another.

Texas quarterback A. Manning finished 12 of 24 for 153 yards, one touchdown and five interceptions. The performance followed his four-touchdown, interception-free game against Miami.

D. Cooper provided the Longhorns’ biggest rushing contribution with 82 yards and a touchdown on eight carries, including a 62-yard run. C. Coleman caught Texas’s touchdown pass.

Both teams had entered the game 6–0 in completed ACC play. TCU now stands at 7–0, while Texas is 6–1.

The Horned Frogs have won every game since their Week 3 loss to LSU. Their latest victory adds a decisive result against a ranked conference opponent to a résumé that already includes California’s only defeat.

For Texas, the loss ends its strongest sustained run of the season. For TCU, it completes the matchup with another win—and a 24-point margin.

headline: LEAVITT HELPS LSU REACH TEN WINS AGAINST TEXAS A&M
body_markdown:
LSU beat Texas A&M 35–21 in Week 13, winning its third consecutive game and improving to 10–2 through its completed schedule.

S. Leavitt completed 21 of 24 passes for 306 yards and three touchdowns without an interception. He also scored a rushing touchdown.

T. Green led LSU with eight catches for 116 yards and a touchdown. M. Clark added five receptions for 109 yards and a score, while R. Mothershed caught the other touchdown pass.

P. Woodland intercepted a pass for the Tigers. X. Atkins and C. Ross II each recorded nine tackles and a sack.

Texas A&M received 231 passing yards and a touchdown from M. Reed, who also ran for 69 yards and two scores. The Aggies fell to 9–3, ending a four-game winning streak.

LSU has now followed its one-point Oklahoma loss with victories over Miami, Florida and Texas A&M.

headline: MCCLAIN’S FOUR PICKS HELP FLORIDA SCORE 80 AGAINST FLORIDA STATE
body_markdown:
Florida answered its loss to LSU with an 80–34 Week 13 victory over Florida State, getting four interceptions from C. McClain.

McClain also recorded 12 tackles and 134 interception-return yards. L. Williams and T. Wallace added one interception apiece, giving the Gators six against Florida State quarterback D. Mensah.

D. Clark supplied an explosive rushing performance: five carries for 121 yards and a touchdown, including an 88-yard run. F. Brandon added three rushing touchdowns and threw for 224 yards and two scores.

M. Mays Jr. caught three passes for 92 yards and a touchdown. D. Wilson added two receptions for 57 yards and the other touchdown catch.

The Gators improved to 9–3 through their completed schedule. Florida State finished the matchup at 3–9.

Florida’s defense produced six takeaways through interceptions and the Gators finished with a 46-point winning margin.

headline: MISSOURI REVERSES CALIFORNIA LOSS, WINS BIG 12 TITLE 24–17
body_markdown:
Missouri turned a rematch into a championship.

The Tigers beat California 24–17 in the Week 15 Big 12 title game, reversing their 52–17 regular-season loss to the Golden Bears. Missouri improved to 9–4 through its completed schedule, while California fell to 11–2 and saw its 10-game winning streak end.

J. Roberts gave Missouri the foundation on the ground, rushing for 186 yards on 16 carries. Four of his attempts gained at least 20 yards, and he averaged 11.6 yards per carry.

The Tigers did not need a high-volume passing game. A. Simmons completed eight of 13 throws for 138 yards and a touchdown without an interception. D. Howerton caught three passes for 124 yards and a score, including an 80-yard reception.

X. Edwards and K. Lanier II each added a rushing touchdown.

Missouri’s defense supplied the other major difference from the first meeting. J. Blair, J. Hancock and K. Louidor-Faustin each intercepted a pass. M. Bryant recorded two sacks, while K. Dean and J. Dowell added one apiece.

California quarterback J. Sagapolutele finished with 329 passing yards and two touchdowns, but also threw three interceptions. D. Thomas caught eight passes for 133 yards and a touchdown, and M. Danzy added five receptions for 81 yards and a score.

The result changes the ending to a stretch in which California had repeatedly overwhelmed opponents. The Golden Bears scored 52 against Missouri in Week 11 and 56 against Stanford in Week 12. In the championship rematch, they finished with 17.

Missouri had entered the title game after a 28–21 loss to Arkansas. Its response delivered both a ninth victory and a conference championship against the team that had beaten it by 35 points earlier in the season.

Missouri next faces Notre Dame in Bowl Week 1. The published Week 17 CFP rankings list the Irish fifth and Missouri 21st. California, listed eighth, is scheduled to face ninth-ranked Florida.

For Missouri, the rematch has supplied a championship and a very different result to carry into the postseason.

headline: OHIO STATE ANSWERS NOTRE DAME, WINS BIG TEN TITLE 41–28
body_markdown:
Ohio State beat Notre Dame 41–28 in the Week 15 Big Ten championship game, reversing its 59–18 loss to the Irish earlier in the season.

The Buckeyes improved to 9–4 with their sixth consecutive victory. Notre Dame fell to 10–3, ending a 10-game winning streak.

J. Sayin completed 17 of 24 passes for 400 yards and four touchdowns with two interceptions. Jeremiah Smith caught nine passes for 188 yards and two scores, earning Big Ten offensive player-of-the-week honors.

B. Jackson contributed 121 rushing yards and two touchdowns, plus six catches for 95 yards and another score. His combined rushing and receiving production totaled 216 yards and three touchdowns.

Ohio State intercepted three passes, one each by R. Pettijohn, K. Harris and D. Sanchez.

Notre Dame received 250 rushing yards from Jonaz Walton, but finished with just 63 passing yards. Ohio State is listed third in the published Week 17 CFP rankings.

headline: BRAY’S 365-YARD TITLE GAME EARNS NATIONAL AND SEC HONORS
body_markdown:
Daniel Bray earned National and SEC offensive player-of-the-week honors after rushing for 365 yards and four touchdowns in Oklahoma’s 49–42 victory over LSU in the Week 15 SEC championship game.

Bray carried 22 times, averaging 16.6 yards per attempt. His longest run covered 85 yards, and five carries gained at least 20.

The Sooners improved to 12–1 through their completed schedule, recording their second win over LSU this season after the 43–42 Week 9 meeting. LSU fell to 10–3.

M. Hawkins Jr. added a rushing touchdown for Oklahoma. Malachi Coleman caught two passes for 88 yards and a touchdown, while T. Keys supplied the other touchdown reception.

LSU received 119 rushing yards from H. Berry and two touchdown catches from T. Green.

Oklahoma is listed second in the published Week 17 CFP rankings.

headline: Florida puts up 50 against No. 1 TCU
body_markdown:
F. Brandon accounted for five touchdowns and Florida beat top-ranked TCU 50–17 in Bowl Week 2, a 33-point win over the team at the head of the published Week 18 CFP rankings.

The Gators entered the matchup ninth in that listing and had already beaten No. 8 California 59–31 in Bowl Week 1. Florida scored 109 points across the two games and improved to 11–3 through its completed schedule. TCU fell to 12–2.

Brandon gave the Horned Frogs trouble on the ground and through the air. He ran 15 times for 115 yards and three touchdowns and completed eight of 12 passes for 222 yards and two scores with one interception. He finished with 337 combined passing and rushing yards.

J. Lloyd turned two catches into 105 yards and a touchdown, with a long reception of 90 yards. J. Baugh caught a 26-yard touchdown pass, D. Wilson added a 50-yard reception and D. Clark ran for 52 yards on five carries. Florida got that production from a passing game that needed just 12 attempts.

On defense, C. McClain returned an interception 66 yards. J. Campbell, J. Woods and T. Wallace each recorded a sack. Florida held TCU to 17 points even as A. Henderson ran for 110 yards on 20 carries.

E. Small accounted for both TCU touchdowns through the air, catching four passes for 116 yards. C. Berger completed 17 of 27 throws for 218 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

The loss ended TCU’s 10-game winning streak. The Horned Frogs had beaten Texas 30–13 in the ACC title game after winning the teams’ regular-season meeting 38–14. Florida had finished the regular season by scoring 80 against Florida State. Its two postseason wins have now come by margins of 28 and 33 points.

headline: Leavitt throws seven touchdowns as LSU beats Notre Dame 70–35
body_markdown:
S. Leavitt threw seven touchdown passes without an interception and LSU beat Notre Dame 70–35 in Bowl Week 2. He completed 20 of 23 passes for 444 yards.

Three Tigers caught two touchdowns apiece. E. Wilson III had four catches for 149 yards, M. Clark had five for 66, and Harlem Berry caught five for 120. Berry added 53 rushing yards and another touchdown, finishing with 173 yards from scrimmage and three scores. T. Green caught the other touchdown pass.

LSU intercepted C. Carr four times and sacked him five times. P. Woodland had two of the interceptions, while C. Ross II and D. Pickett each had one. Jonaz Walton ran for 127 yards and a touchdown for the Irish.

LSU improved to 11–3 through its completed schedule. Notre Dame fell to 11–4 after opening its postseason with a 38–24 win over Missouri.

headline: Blaylock scores twice as Oklahoma beats Texas A&M 28–17
body_markdown:
T. Blaylock scored on the ground and through the air as Oklahoma beat Texas A&M 28–17 in Bowl Week 2. The Sooners improved to 13–1 through their completed schedule.

Blaylock ran 10 times for 39 yards and a touchdown and added a 92-yard touchdown reception. D. Johnson caught a 68-yard touchdown pass, and Malachi Coleman had two catches for 55 yards and a score.

C. Guillory intercepted two passes for Oklahoma, and D. Stone recorded two sacks. Texas A&M’s M. Reed threw for 215 yards and a touchdown and ran for 49 yards and another score. E. Jacobson caught five passes for 49 yards and the Aggies’ receiving touchdown.

Oklahoma has now beaten Texas A&M twice this season. The Sooners won the Week 7 meeting 35–14 and entered the postseason after winning the SEC title.

headline: Penn State beats Florida 38–35 for the BCS title
body_markdown:
Penn State won the 2027 BCS national championship with a 38–35 victory over Florida in Bowl Week 4. The Nittany Lions closed the season with seven straight wins and finished 13–3.

The three-point final capped a four-game postseason run that began with a 38–20 win over UConn. Penn State followed with a 35–28 victory over Ohio State and a 69–28 win over Oklahoma before beating the Gators. Across those four games, the Nittany Lions outscored their opponents 180–111.

P. Falzone threw for 401 yards and four touchdowns against Ohio State. B. Hayes caught eight passes for 119 yards and two scores, while C. Salmin added four catches for 112 yards and a touchdown. J. Peoples ran for 111 yards on 14 carries, and Penn State intercepted three passes.

Peoples supplied the scoring against Oklahoma. He ran for 85 yards on 21 carries and scored five rushing touchdowns. Hayes caught six passes for 283 yards and two touchdowns, and Penn State picked off four passes. M. Neal Jr. had two of the interceptions, with S. Perkins and I. McDaniels collecting one each.

The run started taking shape before bowl season. After consecutive losses to California and Ole Miss left Penn State at 6–3, it beat Florida State, Auburn and Texas Tech by a combined 114–55. The Nittany Lions then won all four of their postseason games, including two decided by a touchdown or less.

Florida finished 12–4. The Gators had scored 59 against California and 50 against TCU earlier in the postseason. They scored 35 in the championship game, the most Penn State allowed in any of its four bowl weeks, but the Nittany Lions still came away with the title.

The season-ending Media rankings put Penn State first with 65 first-place votes and Florida second.

headline: Texas A&M leads the Week 15 recruiting class rankings
body_markdown:
Texas A&M leads the Week 15 rankings for the 2027 recruiting class with 18 commitments and six five-star prospects. Georgia is second with 26 commitments, and LSU is third with 21. The Aggies lead both on class score, with 251.8 points to Georgia’s 243.1 and LSU’s 237.6.

The Aggies’ six five-stars include two quarterbacks and three offensive tackles. Mateo Agasiva and Cornell Awosika are ranked No. 13 and No. 17 nationally. Charles Carraway and Cesar Heredia are both listed at left tackle, while Solomon Bowanko is listed at right tackle. Carraway is No. 11 overall, Heredia No. 15 and Bowanko No. 21. No. 32 Jesse Segal, listed as an athlete, rounds out the six. The class also includes 11 four-stars.

Georgia has 17 four-stars, six more than Texas A&M, and two five-stars. No. 29 Quincy Branham joins previously reported commitment Trey Benavidez, the No. 3 overall prospect. LSU’s five-star group spans three positions: No. 6 defensive tackle Toby Barnes, No. 12 quarterback Damion Ball and No. 31 athlete George Boyko.

Fourth-ranked Oklahoma has commitments from the top two players in the national prospect rankings. Cornerback Brian Sierra of Brookhaven, Mississippi, is No. 1, and edge rusher Wade Scioli of Fort Worth, Texas, is No. 2. The Sooners have four five-stars among 16 commitments. USC rounds out the top five with 24 commitments, including two five-stars.

Penn State and Florida also have commitments near the top of the national board. No. 4 Nick Boone, an edge rusher from the Bronx, is committed to Penn State. Florida has No. 5 Jamal Watkins, a defensive tackle from Ruston, Louisiana, and No. 9 Mohammed Ngata, an edge rusher from Reidsville, North Carolina.

These are commitments in the Week 15 recruiting class. They describe the incoming group for Year 3, with enrollment still to come.

headline: Three Penn State interceptions stand out in the title-game box
body_markdown:
Penn State intercepted three passes in its 38–35 national championship win over Florida. J. Joseph, D. Leach and S. Perkins each picked off F. Brandon, and Leach added eight tackles.

P. Falzone threw for 275 yards and two touchdowns on 14 of 24 passing and ran for another score. D. James caught four passes for 115 yards and a touchdown, while D. Fleming had seven catches for 99 yards and a score.

C. Wallace added 87 rushing yards on 19 carries and 61 receiving yards on three catches, finishing with 148 yards from scrimmage. Q. Martin Jr. ran for 28 yards and a touchdown on four carries.

Brandon threw one touchdown and ran for two for Florida. D. Wilson caught the scoring pass and finished with four receptions for 60 yards.

headline: Brandon throws four touchdowns as Florida beats LSU 41–14
body_markdown:
F. Brandon threw four touchdown passes and Florida intercepted five passes in a 41–14 win over LSU in Bowl Week 3. The victory sent the Gators into the national championship game.

Brandon completed 16 of 25 passes for 267 yards with two interceptions. M. Mays Jr. caught seven passes for 100 yards and two touchdowns, while D. Wilson and T. Abrams each caught a scoring pass. J. Lloyd added four receptions for 96 yards.

K. Brown had two interceptions for Florida. M. Graham, J. Lyons and T. Harris added one apiece. LSU’s S. Leavitt threw for 195 yards, with J. Harris catching his touchdown pass.

The result gave Florida a win in the rematch after LSU had beaten the Gators 45–35 in Week 12.

headline: Colorado and Houston list new head coaches as offseason recruiting opens
body_markdown:
Colorado and Houston entered the first week of offseason recruiting with different names atop their coaching staffs. Colorado now lists Brian Norris Jr. as head coach, replacing Benji Aboushi in the league’s coaching listings. Houston lists Curt Vernon in place of Itachi Uchiha.

Norris takes over a Colorado program that went 1–11 in Year 2, including 0–7 in conference play. His coaching profile lists a Power Spread offense and a 4–2–5 defense, with a 0–0 career record. The Buffaloes had 66 players listed in the first offseason recruiting week, down from 84 at the end of the season.

Vernon’s profile lists a 10–14 career record, a Pro Style offense and a 3–3–5 defense. Houston went 3–9 in Year 2 and won one of its seven conference games. The Cougars had 64 players listed entering offseason recruiting, down from 80 at the end of the season.

The two programs enter the offseason with similar roster counts after different seasons on the field. Colorado’s count fell by 18 and Houston’s by 16. Across the 32 tracked teams, the number of players listed fell from 2,570 to 2,268 after the Players Leaving stage. Those counts describe the rosters at the start of offseason recruiting, while teams are still assembling their Year 3 groups.

The latest published high school recruiting standings still come from Week 15. Texas A&M led that class with 18 commitments, including six five-stars, followed by Georgia and LSU. The opening of offseason recruiting gives Colorado and Houston their next opportunity to add to the rosters their new coaches inherit. For now, the first offseason update shows who is listed in charge and how many players each program has on hand.

headline: Oklahoma, Louisville and California show the biggest signing-day roster drops
body_markdown:
Oklahoma, Louisville and California had the largest drops in listed players among 32 BCS teams as the league reached National Signing Day. The three programs had 73 fewer players listed between Offseason Recruiting Week 3 and Signing Day. Across the 32 teams, the count fell from 2,268 to 1,755, with 31 teams showing smaller rosters.

Oklahoma’s count went from 79 to 53, a drop of 26. Cornerback E. Bowen and left tackle M. Fasusi, both listed at 99 overall in the previous update, were absent from the Signing Day roster. The Sooners still listed right tackle A. Babalola at 95, right guard E. Pierre-Louis at 93 and wide receiver T. Keys at 92. Oklahoma won the SEC title in Year 2, and two of its highest-rated players on the current roster are on the offensive line.

Louisville went from 73 listed players to 49. Safety K. Entringer and receiver L. McCoy, each previously rated 87, were absent from the new list. Running back O. Kromah remained at 90 overall, with tight end J. Miles and receiver J. Moore both listed at 84.

California went from 67 players to 44. Receiver M. Danzy, previously rated 92, and tight end D. Thomas, previously rated 91, were absent. The Golden Bears still listed receiver V. Spafford at 90 and quarterback J. Sagapolutele at 89.

LSU, Ole Miss and Colorado each had 22 fewer players listed. Tennessee was the only team whose count held steady, at 58. Oregon had 72 players listed, the most among the 32 teams, while South Carolina had 41.

The counts describe the rosters available at Signing Day. Individual reasons for absences and the enrollment of incoming recruits remain unconfirmed.

headline: BCS opens Year 3 preseason with Penn State as defending champion
body_markdown:
The BCS has moved into its third season. Commissioner Burnie confirmed on November 15 that the league is in preseason for the 2028 campaign. The league has yet to specify a numbered week for the new season. As of November 16, the results on the league website still reflected the end of the 2027 season.

Penn State enters Year 3 as the defending national champion after beating Florida 38–35 in the 2027 title game. The Nittany Lions finished 13–3, while the Gators finished 12–4, according to their completed schedules. Texas A&M won the inaugural BCS championship a season earlier, beating LSU 31–25. The league has had a different champion in each of its first two seasons.

Penn State’s run gave the new season a clear benchmark. The Nittany Lions beat Ohio State 35–28 in the playoff, then put up 69 points in a 69–28 semifinal win over Oklahoma. Their last three wins came by seven, 41 and three points, respectively. The title game was their tightest finish of that stretch.

Florida took a different route to the final. The Gators beat TCU 50–17 and LSU 41–14, allowing just 31 points across those two games. Penn State scored 38 in the championship alone. Oklahoma finished 13–2 after its semifinal loss, while LSU finished 11–4, leaving both semifinalists with double-digit wins.

The calendar change puts those results in the books and turns attention to the first 2028 matchups. The defending champions and the two teams they beat in the last two rounds all finished 2027 with at least nine wins, while Florida came within a field goal of matching Penn State on the scoreboard. Those are the results the contenders carry into preseason. The first 2028 schedule and rankings will give the new season its own starting point.

headline: Joyner’s six touchdowns lift TCU past California, 76–70
body_markdown:
TCU opened its 2028 season with a 76–70 win over California, surviving a game that produced 146 points and two extraordinary individual performances.

Q.Joyner carried the Horned Frogs with 280 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 18 attempts. He added eight catches for 150 yards and two more scores, finishing with 430 yards from scrimmage and six touchdowns. His longest run covered 81 yards, and his longest reception went for 75.

California answered with a huge receiving day from C.Burns, who caught 12 passes for 304 yards and seven touchdowns. Even that production left the Golden Bears six points short in a matchup the published Week 0 Media Top 25 had listed as No. 10 California against No. 4 TCU.

Joyner supplied 36 points through his six touchdowns alone. He averaged more than 15 yards per carry and accounted for 150 of TCU’s 393 passing yards through his work as a receiver. The Horned Frogs had another major target in E.Small, who caught six passes for 159 yards and two touchdowns.

T.Burgess threw four touchdown passes and added two rushing scores for TCU. His 35 rushing yards complemented Joyner’s production, giving the Horned Frogs scoring contributions from both positions on the ground.

The defensive numbers were just as consequential in a game with so little margin. M.Strickland intercepted two passes, while J.Angerer and E.Hill IV added one apiece. California recorded two interceptions of its own, credited to K.Scales and N.Chandler.

TCU’s completed schedule now stands at 1–0, while California starts 0–1. The teams’ published poll records still showed 0–0 at the time of the Week 0 rankings.

Both face immediate tests in Week 1. TCU is scheduled to host Florida, while California hosts Alabama. For the Horned Frogs, the opening win comes with a clear defensive challenge after allowing 70 points. California’s offense has already shown how much damage it can do, but its next game arrives with a loss to recover from.

headline: Virginia Tech picks off six passes in 63–28 win over Texas
body_markdown:
Virginia Tech opened 2028 with a 63–28 victory over Texas, pairing a 35-point winning margin with six interceptions.

J.Scott and A.Fanene intercepted two passes apiece. G.Williams and K.Moore added one each, matching the six interceptions charged to the Texas passers.

R.Poling led the Hokies’ receivers with seven catches for 153 yards and three touchdowns. S.White-Helton added three catches for 102 yards and a touchdown, giving Virginia Tech two receivers above 100 yards.

Texas had 71 rushing yards from D.Cooper and 70 from F.Meadows, but finished the opener 0–1. Virginia Tech moves to 1–0 and has Nebraska next on its Week 1 schedule.

The published Week 0 Media Top 25 listed Texas at No. 11 before the completed result.

headline: Alabama opens with 37–31 win over Georgia
body_markdown:
Alabama began the 2028 season with a 37–31 victory over Georgia in a matchup the published Week 0 Media Top 25 listed as No. 18 against No. 12.

D.Redeaux rushed for 118 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries, including an 81-yard run. G.Boss threw for 178 yards and three touchdowns, with scoring receptions credited to E.Crowell, W.Watkins Jr. and J.Lopez.

Alabama’s defense intercepted four passes. E.Gonzalez, J.Edwards, X.Griffin and C.McDonald III each recorded one. Griffin also had two sacks.

Georgia received 134 rushing yards and a touchdown from J.Leon on 18 carries, but starts 0–1. Alabama moves to 1–0 before a Week 1 trip to California, which lost its opener 76–70 to TCU.

headline: Washington wins at Texas A&M as Penn State opens with a rout
body_markdown:
Washington opened the 2028 season with a 45–35 victory at Texas A&M, giving the Huskies an immediate road win behind four touchdown passes from T.McMillan.

McMillan completed 27 of 38 throws for 380 yards, with one interception. D.Roebuck was his leading target, catching eight passes for 182 yards and three touchdowns. His longest reception covered 61 yards.

The Huskies also got rushing touchdowns from B.Bonner Jr. and J.Clay. Bonner ran for 65 yards on 14 carries and added 40 receiving yards, while Clay finished with 28 rushing yards and 15 through the air. Together, they supplied the ground scores that complemented McMillan’s passing production.

Texas A&M had enough offense to keep the score within 10 points, with C.Dyer throwing for 382 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. J.Myles caught seven passes for 123 yards, and T.Favors turned two receptions into 96 yards and a touchdown. K.Edwards added 80 rushing yards and a score.

Washington’s pass rush recorded five sacks, including 2½ from D.Colman-Brusa. Texas A&M’s T.Bell III finished with 13 tackles, but the Aggies begin the season 0–1. Washington starts 1–0.

The next test for Texas A&M is a trip to defending national champion Penn State, which opened with a 55–16 win at LSU. The Nittany Lions’ 39-point victory makes that Week 1 matchup a demanding assignment for an Aggies team looking to avoid a second straight loss.

Q.Martin Jr. ran for 191 yards and two touchdowns on just 12 carries for Penn State, including an 85-yard run. P.Falzone completed 14 of 19 passes for 221 yards and four touchdowns. D.Vonnahme caught six passes for 79 yards and two scores, while S.Perkins intercepted two passes.

Penn State enters the Texas A&M game 1–0. LSU starts 0–1 and is scheduled to visit Texas in Week 1. Both the Nittany Lions and Huskies have their opening wins secured; the Aggies and Tigers already face the task of responding to a defeat.

headline: USC opens with 38–13 win over Oregon
body_markdown:
USC began its 2028 season with a 38–13 victory over Oregon, getting touchdowns from three different rushers and holding the Ducks to 10 net rushing yards.

A.Clemons ran for 74 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries. Quarterback S.Tongue added 60 rushing yards and a score, while L.Herrien supplied another rushing touchdown.

Tongue also completed 25 of 35 passes for 271 yards and two touchdowns, with one interception. K.Dixon-Wyatt and J.Ferguson caught the scoring passes. R.Kusch led USC’s receivers with eight catches for 92 yards.

The Trojans recorded four sacks, including 1½ from R.Mangum. Oregon quarterback A.Hill threw for 192 yards and a touchdown but finished with minus-15 rushing yards. USC starts 1–0, while Oregon falls to 0–1.

headline: Ole Miss beats Miami 42–28 behind four Knight touchdown passes
body_markdown:
Ole Miss opened 2028 with a 42–28 road victory over Miami, led by four touchdown passes from D.Knight and seven sacks from its defense.

Knight completed 14 of 21 attempts for 227 yards, with two interceptions. Tight ends T.Jewel and M.Smith caught two touchdowns apiece. Jewel finished with three catches for 112 yards, including a 71-yard reception.

L.Jackson led the pass rush with 3½ sacks and four tackles for loss. Ole Miss also intercepted two passes, matching the two interceptions charged to Miami quarterback A.Carlisle.

Miami got 113 rushing yards from G.Pringle Jr. and 112 from Carlisle, but begins 0–1. Ole Miss starts 1–0 and is scheduled to host Pittsburgh in Week 1, while Miami visits Michigan.

headline: McNabb throws 10 touchdowns as Oklahoma overwhelms Ohio State, 79–27
body_markdown:
Oklahoma delivered a forceful early-season result with a 79–27 victory at Ohio State, riding 10 touchdown passes from D.McNabb in a Week 1 matchup listed by the published Media Top 25 as No. 3 against No. 1.

McNabb completed 26 of 33 passes for 504 yards without an interception. Four receivers caught his touchdown throws, with E.Thomas leading the group on eight receptions for 217 yards and four scores.

D.Carter added eight catches for 60 yards and three touchdowns. P.Livingstone caught four passes for 43 yards and two scores, while T.Keys supplied two catches for 76 yards and the remaining receiving touchdown. McNabb also scored once on the ground.

The result moves Oklahoma to 2–0 after its 77–3 opening win at South Carolina. Through two completed games, the Sooners have scored 156 points and allowed 30, winning by 74 and 52 points.

Ohio State had opened with a 52–24 victory at Missouri, but its home opener brought a much different outcome. The Buckeyes fall to 1–1 despite a huge rushing performance from G.Mayweather, who carried 17 times for 232 yards and two touchdowns. His longest run covered 91 yards.

Oklahoma’s defense intercepted three passes, with T.Haynes, B.Womack and C.Guillory recording one apiece. J.Kreul contributed 3½ sacks, while Womack finished with 11 tackles.

Ohio State used two passers. B.Underwood threw for 159 yards and two touchdowns with three interceptions, while T.St. Clair added 53 passing yards without a touchdown or interception. C.Henry Jr. led the Buckeyes’ receivers with six catches for 101 yards.

The rankings attached to the matchup describe the field before the completed result. Oklahoma’s immediate statement is on the scoreboard: a 52-point road victory over the team listed first, following another decisive road win in its opener. The Sooners have paired two prolific scoring games with a defense that has yet to allow more than 27 points.

headline: Joyner runs for 307 yards as TCU edges Florida, 45–42
body_markdown:
TCU followed its 76–70 opening win over California with another narrow victory, beating Florida 45–42 at home in Week 1.

Q.Joyner ran for 307 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries, including an 87-yard run. T.Burgess threw three touchdown passes, two to E.Small and one to D.Ezukanma. Small finished with three catches for 89 yards.

Florida quarterback F.Brandon completed 24 of 33 passes for 404 yards and four touchdowns, with two interceptions. S.Terry II caught seven passes for 100 yards and three scores, then added two rushing touchdowns.

TCU moves to 2–0 with its wins coming by six and three points. Florida falls to 1–1. The Horned Frogs next visit Louisville, while Florida travels to Notre Dame in Week 2.

headline: Pittsburgh opens with 24–21 road win over Ole Miss
body_markdown:
Pittsburgh began its 2028 season with a 24–21 victory at Ole Miss, handing the Rebels their first loss after their opening win at Miami.

R.Marriott completed four of five passes for 72 yards and a touchdown without an interception. T.Robinson caught the scoring pass for 40 yards, while T.Ballard added a rushing touchdown.

Pittsburgh’s defense intercepted D.Knight twice, with D.Johnson and D.Gardner recording one each. Knight finished with 190 passing yards and two touchdown throws. J.Osborne ran for 93 yards and a touchdown and added a receiving score for Ole Miss.

The Panthers start 1–0, while the Rebels move to 1–1. Pittsburgh is scheduled to host Colorado in Week 2.
